title: What if UCLA became the number-one university?
narrator: Sports announcer: excited play-by-play, as if this were a championship broadcast. Big energy, clean diction on names and numbers.
basedOn: content/v07_ucla_number_one/storyboard.md (PR #11) and the brief's Fun take
logline: A made-up leaderboard, called like a championship game. UCLA takes the top spot; parking stays impossible.

cues.onScreen: What if UCLA became number one?
cues.narration: What if UCLA became number one?

cues.onScreen: This is UCLA: Royce Hall, sun, blue and gold.
cues.narration: UCLA! Royce Hall, sunshine, blue and gold, since 1919!

cues.onScreen: In real rankings, it's high. Not first.
cues.narration: In real rankings? Very high. Just not first.
But tonight, on a totally made-up leaderboard...
UCLA is climbing! Past one school! Past another! The rest of the list slides down one row!

cues.onScreen: Until it knocks the top school off the board.
cues.narration: And it takes the top spot! Unbelievable scenes in Westwood!

cues.onScreen: Problem 1: Even more applications pour in.
cues.narration: Applications: already a mountain. Now it's a mountain range.

cues.onScreen: Problem 2: USC is not taking this well.
cues.narration: Rivalry week: across town, USC would like to file a complaint.

cues.onScreen: Problem 3: Campus tours need a waitlist.
cues.narration: Tour season: the tour now has a waitlist. Parking is still impossible.

cues.onScreen: So UCLA throws a party in Westwood.
cues.narration: Westwood celebrates! Traffic on Wilshire: unchanged!

notes: The leaderboard is fictional (v07.a.ranking). The script never names a real ranking or a real position; keep it that way on screen.

The fact pack for this video is still a draft (verified: false). Numbers spoken here match its values, but confirm them before recording: founded 1919 (v07.f.founded). 'Already a mountain' of applications is deliberately vague until v07.f.applications is checked.
Narrator: sports announcer, as recommended for the two competition videos (V07 and V12).
